title: Rust: Simple Calculator
description: Build a simple calculator that performs basic operations.

steps.title: Add Two Numbers
steps.description: Write a function `add(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64` that returns the sum. Call with 10.5 and 20.3, print result.
hints: `fn add(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 { a + b }`

steps.title: Subtract, Multiply, Divide
steps.description: Write functions for subtract, multiply, and divide. Call each with (20, 4) and print results.

steps.title: Calculator with Match
steps.description: Write a function `calculate(a: f64, b: f64, op: char) -> f64` that uses match to select the operation. Test with (10, 3, '+') and (10, 3, '-').

steps.title: Division by Zero
steps.description: Handle division by zero gracefully. Modify `calculate` to return `Option<f64>` — `Some(result)` on success, `None` on division by zero.
hints: If op is '/' and b == 0.0, return `None`.
Print using match: `Some(v) => println!("{}", v), None => println!("Error: division by zero")`

verification.failureMessage: Print 10/2=5 and error for division by zero.

steps.title: Interactive Calculator
steps.description: Evaluate `(15 + 3) * 2 - 8 / 4` by chaining multiple calculate calls. Calculate step by step and print the result.
